extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO filing staff seeking accelerated examination under the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for requesting and obtaining expedited examination at the USPTO under the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) program, including form requirements, national-stage considerations under 35 U.S.C. 371, and PPH eXtra timing targets. Covers Global/IP5 pilots and bilateral PPH arrangements with other offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core PPH eligibility (allowable claim in first office)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant receives a ruling from a first patent office that at least one claim is allowable, the applicant may request fast track examination of corresponding claim(s) in a corresponding patent application pending in a second participating patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH "allows applicants who receive a determination of allowable claims in an application from one Intellectual Property (IP) office to obtain expedited examination of corresponding claims filed in an application pending in another participating IP Office." Use the work product of the first office (PCT or national) as the basis for requesting PPH status at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the correct PPH request form (Global/IP5 or bilateral)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH requests must be filed on the appropriate request form: the consolidated Global/IP5 form (SB/20GLBL) for participating pilot offices or the country-specific bilateral forms where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since January 6, 2014, pilots simplified access with one form for participating countries. The USPTO participates in both Global PPH and IP5 PPH pilots so applicants need not specify which pilot is used. For bilateral participants not in Global PPH, applicants must use the special national forms (e.g., SB/20BH, SB/20CZ, SB/20FR, etc.). Links to request forms for each bilateral PPH program are provided on the USPTO page.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 371 national stage express request requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For U.S. national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, the PPH request form was modified (October 2022) to include an express request to begin national stage processing under 35 U.S.C. 371(f); that express request must be made for immediate national stage processing to begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants use older PPH forms that do not expressly request to begin national stage processing under 35 U.S.C. 371(f), processing will not begin until expiration of the PCT Article 22(1) or (2) or PCT Article 39(1)(a) time limits (i.e., 30 months from the earliest priority date), even if a PPH request was granted. A September 2023 review found only 50% used the newer form, causing delays. For questions contact the PCT Helpdesk or PPHfeedback@uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee for PPH participation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fee under the PPH programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO notes explicitly: "There is no fee under the PPH programs." Further procedural or policy notices are referenced (Federal Register notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH eXtra performance targets (timing goals for office actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating offices have set target deadlines for issuing office actions on PPH applications to make timing more predictable (the PPH eXtra initiative). Targets differ by office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office-specific targets: USPTO target—average period from completion of PPH request to first office action on the merits: within 6 months (revised effective January 1, 2026); average period from applicant's response to the first office action on the merits to subsequent office action: within 3 months. APO, CNIPA, JPO, ILPO, MOIP, and PRH target an average period from completion of PPH request to first office action within 3 months and average period from applicant's response to subsequent office action within 3 months. Goals will be reviewed and updated annually. Office-specific results are published where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH status may be based on earlier positive work product (PCT or national)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any earlier positive results (whether PCT or national work product) from participating IP offices may form the basis for PPH status at the USPTO under the simplified pilot programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Global PPH and IP5 PPH pilot requirements are substantially identical, USPTO applicants may file a PPH request based on the work product of any office participating in either pilot. The page emphasizes strategic possibilities for IP owners in leveraging earlier allowable determinations from many offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and equity consideration in PPH handling
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO has adjusted docketing of PPH applications with a granted petition to align PPH and non-PPH pendency times more proportionately by technology area, to preserve equity among applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO observed that PPH applications constituted about 2% of filings with shorter first action pendency (~7.5 months) while non-PPH pendency increased to over 22 months; to avoid disproportionate expedited benefits, USPTO revised docketing so PPH first action pendency in a technology area is approximately half the non-PPH pendency and updated the PPH eXtra target for first action (see timing targets). The USPTO states this is to sustain long-term value and equitable examination for all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating offices and bilateral agreements (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH participation depends on whether the other office is a Global/IP5 participant or has a bilateral PPH agreement with the USPTO; applicants must follow the applicable program rules and forms for that pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists Global/IP5 participating offices and bilateral PPH participants (e.g., Bahrain, Czech Republic, France, Mexico, Malaysia, Morocco, Nicaragua, Philippines, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Taiwan, etc.) and provides links to the specific request forms and notices for each program. For offices not in the Global pilot, use the country-specific forms indicated on the USPTO page.
